lesson_scope: Line-plane intersection parameter determination, position vector calculations, parallel line-plane non-intersection proofs, line containment in planes, foot of perpendicular from point to plane, laser reflections, ratio division of segments, and 3D pyramid sectioning.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Direct parameter solving for line-plane intersection.

hints: Express the line in parametric form: $x = 1 + 2\lambda, y = 2 + \lambda, z = -1 + 3\lambda$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute the parametric coordinates of the line into the plane equation:
$$2(1 + 2\lambda) + 3(2 + \lambda) - (-1 + 3\lambda) = 17$$

Expand and collect like terms:
$$2 + 4\lambda + 6 + 3\lambda + 1 - 3\lambda = 17$$
$$4\lambda + 9 = 17 \implies 4\lambda = 8 \implies \lambda = 2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes line parametric coordinates into plane.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Position vector evaluation from parameter.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Position vector evaluation from line parameter.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $\lambda = 2$ into the vector line equation:
$$\mathbf{r}_P = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} + 2\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + 4 \\ 2 + 2 \\ -1 + 6 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 4 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$$

hints: Since $\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{n} = 0$, line direction is parallel to the plane.
Test base point $(1, 2, -1)$ in plane: $2(1) - 2 - (-1) = 1 \neq 8$. Conclude no intersection.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the scalar product between line direction and plane normal:
$$\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} \cdot \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} = 2(2) + 1(-1) + 3(-1) = 4 - 1 - 3 = 0$$
Since $\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{n} = 0$, the line is parallel to the plane.

Test whether the base point $(1, 2, -1)$ lies on the plane:
$$2(1) - 1(2) - 1(-1) = 2 - 2 + 1 = 1 \neq 8$$
Because the base point does not satisfy the plane equation, the line is strictly parallel to the plane and never intersects it.

ai_rubric.observable: Shows base point $1 \neq 8$ and concludes no intersection.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Line containment within a plane.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Line contained entirely in plane proof.

hints: Conclude that the line lies entirely within the plane.

walkthrough.text:
Show that the line direction is orthogonal to the normal vector:
$$\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{n} = 2(3) + (-1)(1) + 1(-5) = 6 - 1 - 5 = 0$$

Show that the base point $(1, 2, -3)$ lies on the plane:
$$3(1) + 1(2) - 5(-3) = 3 + 2 + 15 = 20$$
Since the line is parallel to the plane and contains a point lying on the plane, the entire line $l$ lies within $\Pi$.

ai_rubric.observable: Concludes line lies entirely in plane.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Distance along line from base point.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the displacement vector $\vec{AP}$:
$$\vec{AP} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 - 1 \\ 4 - 2 \\ 5 - (-1) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 2 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$$

Calculate the magnitude of $\vec{AP}$:
$$AP = |\vec{AP}| = \sqrt{4^2 + 2^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{56} = 2\sqrt{14}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Foot of perpendicular from point onto plane.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foot of perpendicular from point to plane.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the normal line through $A(1, 2, 3)$ with direction $\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + \lambda \\ 2 + 2\lambda \\ 3 + 2\lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

Substitute into the plane equation to find $\lambda$:
$$(1 + \lambda) + 2(2 + 2\lambda) + 2(3 + 2\lambda) = 20$$
$$9\lambda + 11 = 20 \implies 9\lambda = 9 \implies \lambda = 1$$

Calculate the coordinates of foot $F$:
$$F = (1 + 1, 2 + 2(1), 3 + 2(1)) = (2, 4, 5)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Core: Piercing intersection point and line segment distance.

walkthrough.text:
Write the line equation in parametric form:
$$\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 + \lambda \\ 1 + 3\lambda \\ 2 + 2\lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

Substitute into the plane equation $x + 2y - z = 7$:
$$(-3 + \lambda) + 2(1 + 3\lambda) - (2 + 2\lambda) = 7$$
$$-3 + \lambda + 2 + 6\lambda - 2 - 2\lambda = 7 \implies 5\lambda - 3 = 7 \implies 5\lambda = 10 \implies \lambda = 2$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Position vector and exact distance proof.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $\lambda = 2$ into the line equation to find $\mathbf{r}_P$:
$$\mathbf{r}_P = \begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} + 2\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 7 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$$

Calculate the distance $DP$:
$$DP = |\vec{DP}| = 2|\mathbf{d}| = 2\sqrt{1^2 + 3^2 + 2^2} = 2\sqrt{14}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Core: Perpendicular bisector plane intersecting line.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the midpoint of segment $AB$:
$$M = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 1 + 3 \\ 2 + 1 \\ -1 + 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1.5 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the normal vector $\mathbf{n} = \vec{AB}$ and evaluate constant $d$:
$$\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 - 1 \\ 1 - 2 \\ 1 - (-1) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$d = 2(2) - 1(1.5) + 2(0) = 2.5 \implies 4x - 2y + 4z = 5$$

Substitute parametric coordinates of $l$ into $4x - 2y + 4z = 5$:
$$4(1 + \mu) - 2(1 - \mu) + 4(2 - 4\mu) = 5$$
$$4 + 4\mu - 2 + 2\mu + 8 - 16\mu = 5 \implies 10 - 10\mu = 5 \implies 10\mu = 5 \implies \mu = \frac{1}{2}$$

Compute the position vector of intersection point $P$:
$$\mathbf{r}_P = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + 0.5 \\ 1 - 0.5 \\ 2 - 4(0.5) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1.5 \\ 0.5 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{3}{2}\mathbf{i} + \frac{1}{2}\mathbf{j}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Core: Parallel distinct vs line containment in plane.

parts.label: (a)
hints: Conclude line $l_1$ is parallel to $\Pi$ and does not intersect.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the scalar product of the line direction and plane normal:
$$\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} \cdot \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} = 4 - 1 - 3 = 0$$

Test the base point $(1, 2, -1)$ in the plane equation:
$$2(1) - 2 - (-1) = 1 \neq 8$$
Since the direction is parallel to the plane but no point lies on the plane, line $l_1$ does not intersect $\Pi$.

parts.label: (b)
hints: Conclude that line $l_2$ lies entirely within plane $\Pi$.

walkthrough.text:
Confirm that the direction of $l_2$ is orthogonal to the normal:
$$\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} \cdot \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} = 0$$

Test whether the base point $(5, 2, 0)$ lies in plane $\Pi$:
$$2(5) - 2 - 0 = 8 = 8$$
Since $\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{n} = 0$ and the base point lies in the plane, every point on line $l_2$ lies in plane $\Pi$.

ai_rubric.observable: Concludes line lies entirely in plane.

questions.difficulty_reason: Core: Normal line, foot of perpendicular, and exact distance.

walkthrough.text:
Extract the normal vector $\mathbf{n}$ from the plane equation:
$$\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Write the equation of the normal line $l_N$ through $A(2, 3, 1)$:
$$\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} + \lambda \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foot of perpendicular and distance calculation.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute the parametric coordinates into the plane equation:
$$2(2 + 2\lambda) + 2(3 + 2\lambda) - (1 - \lambda) = 18$$
$$4 + 4\lambda + 6 + 4\lambda - 1 + \lambda = 18 \implies 9\lambda + 9 = 18 \implies \lambda = 1$$

Find the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular $F$:
$$F = (2 + 2(1), 3 + 2(1), 1 - 1) = (4, 5, 0)$$

Calculate the perpendicular distance:
$$\text{Distance} = |\vec{AF}| = \sqrt{(4-2)^2 + (5-3)^2 + (0-1)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 4 + 1} = 3$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Capstone: Laser ray plane strike and floor reflection intersection.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute the parametric coordinates of the laser beam into plane $\Pi$:
$$(-1 + 2\lambda) + 2(5 - \lambda) + 2(7 - 2\lambda) = 11$$
$$-1 + 2\lambda + 10 - 2\lambda + 14 - 4\lambda = 11$$
$$23 - 4\lambda = 11 \implies 4\lambda = 12 \implies \lambda = 3$$

Compute the coordinates of strike point $P$:
$$P = (-1 + 2(3), 5 - 3, 7 - 2(3)) = (5, 2, 1)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes line coordinates into mirror plane.

walkthrough.text:
State the equation of the reflected line $l_R$:
$$\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} + \mu \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -3 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$$

Set the $z$-component equal to $0$ for the horizontal floor plane:
$$1 - 4\mu = 0 \implies 4\mu = 1 \implies \mu = \frac{1}{4}$$

Evaluate the coordinates of strike point $Q$:
$$Q = \left(5 + 0, 2 - 3\left(\frac{1}{4}\right), 0\right) = \left(5, \frac{5}{4}, 0\right) = (5, 1.25, 0)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Capstone: Segment ratio division by a plane.

walkthrough.text:
Find the vector equation of the line passing through $A(4, -1, 3)$ and $B(-2, 5, -3)$:
$$\vec{AB} = \begin{pmatrix} -2 - 4 \\ 5 - (-1) \\ -3 - 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -6 \\ 6 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix} = 6\begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} \implies \mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 - \lambda \\ -1 + \lambda \\ 3 - \lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

Substitute parametric coordinates into plane $\Pi: 2x - y + 3z = 6$:
$$2(4 - \lambda) - (-1 + \lambda) + 3(3 - \lambda) = 6$$
$$8 - 2\lambda + 1 - \lambda + 9 - 3\lambda = 6 \implies 18 - 6\lambda = 6 \implies 6\lambda = 12 \implies \lambda = 2$$

Compute the coordinates of point $P$:
$$P = (4 - 2, -1 + 2, 3 - 2) = (2, 1, 1)$$

Compute displacement vectors $\vec{AP}$ and $\vec{PB}$:
$$\vec{AP} = \mathbf{p} - \mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 - 4 \\ 1 - (-1) \\ 1 - 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ 2 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\vec{PB} = \mathbf{b} - \mathbf{p} = \begin{pmatrix} -2 - 2 \\ 5 - 1 \\ -3 - 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 4 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compare the magnitudes and vector ratios:
$$\vec{PB} = 2\begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ 2 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix} = 2\vec{AP}$$
Therefore, point $P$ divides the line segment $AB$ internally in the exact ratio $1 : 2$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Capstone: Pyramid slicing plane, edge penetration point, and cross-sectional area.

walkthrough.text: The base of the pyramid lies in the plane $z = 0$, and the apex is $V(2, 2, 6)$ with height $z = 6$.

At half its vertical height, $z = \frac{6}{2} = 3$.
Since the plane is horizontal and parallel to the base, its Cartesian equation is:
$$z = 3$$

Set the $z$-component of line $l_{VC}$ equal to $3$:
$$6 - 3\mu = 3 \implies 3\mu = 3 \implies \mu = 1$$

Compute the coordinates of penetration point $K$:
$$K = (2 + 1(1), 2 + 1(1), 6 - 3(1)) = (3, 3, 3)$$

parts.label: (c)
hints: Since the slicing plane is at half height, the cross-section is a square of side length $\frac{4}{2} = 2$.

walkthrough.text:
Verify that $K$ is the midpoint of sloping edge $VC$:
$$\text{Midpoint}(VC) = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 2 + 4 \\ 2 + 4 \\ 6 + 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 3 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} = K$$

Compute the side length and area of the square cross-section:
By similar triangles, at half the height of the pyramid, the side length of the square cross-section is half the base side length:
$$\text{Side length } s = \frac{4}{2} = 2$$
$$\text{Area} = s^2 = 2^2 = 4$$
